nodes.plm_action: Remove the label
nodes.plm_caption:
This video captures a man's attempts to create a mermaid costume for his doll. Starting with doll clothes, he cuts along the lines to shape, and finishes with a mermaid tail made of cardboard. The man has a tattoo on his left arm.
The background includes a glass cabinet displaying many porcelain items, and a wooden box and some chairs in the room.
There is no additional context or description available in the transcription.

summary.brief: A man demonstrates how to cut, label, and finish the paper pattern for a BJD doll corset.
summary.detailed: The presenter, a man in a red shirt with a pentagram tattoo on his left forearm, removes a yellow‑gauze cast from a miniature doll and cuts the back of the cast in half. He then slices the remaining paper into the individual corset pieces, turning some face‑up and others face‑down as required. Each piece is numbered sequentially from the front (1, 2, 3, …) and arrows are drawn to indicate the correct orientation. He adds seam‑allowance lines based on his sewing‑machine allowance, then cuts the pieces precisely along those lines. After the pattern is prepared, he shows a row of five yellow paper strips, counts them while pointing, and holds up a shoe for comparison. The tutorial concludes with a close‑up of him holding a Barbie doll while looking away.

action.detailed: Cut the cast in half, slice the paper into individual corset components, number and mark each piece with orientation arrows and seam‑allowance lines, then cut out the finalized pattern pieces.
action.actor: The presenter, a man wearing a red shirt with a pentagram tattoo on his left forearm

At the beginning of the video, the mannequin's legs and waist are visible. He holds it on the upper abdomen with both hands. It is then wrapped with a yellow bandage. As he starts cutting it with scissors, only the left arm and hand are visible.
This video takes place indoors. Behind the mannequin are glass shelves on the wall. The walls are cream colored and the switch plates are white. There is a framed picture on the left wall.

summary.brief: Man creates a paper corset pattern for a doll.
summary.detailed: The presenter first removes the paper cast that was wrapped around the doll, then cuts the middle of the back piece and separates each section into two opposite‑facing halves. He numbers every piece, adds arrows to indicate orientation, and draws the seam lines along with extra seam‑allowance margins directly on the paper. After pulling off the plastic backing, he adds a few extra guide lines for shaping, shows the basic layout of the pattern, and finishes by confirming the pattern is ready for the next step.

action.detailed: Cut the cast, split the back into halves, number and label each piece, draw seam lines and seam‑allowance margins, and prepare the paper pattern for fabric cutting.
action.actor: the man in a red shirt with a pentagram tattoo on his left forearm

summary.brief: A man in a red shirt trims a paper cast and other materials from a doll, numbers the pattern pieces, and marks a mask.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a man wearing a red shirt and a goatee standing at a table while a doll in a white skirt is visible on the surface and shelves line the background. He lifts a paper cast that has been placed on the doll and, using a pair of scissors, cuts the middle of the back to separate the front and back sections. He then halves the cast so that each half mirrors the other, removes excess material, and cuts out the individual pattern pieces. While the pieces are still on the table he numbers them in order, adds arrows to indicate orientation, and trims seam‑allowance strips. Later the camera shows him cutting a white wig or hair from the mannequin with scissors, using pliers to detach the head, and clearing remaining cream‑colored material. The footage then shifts to brief close‑up clips of him cutting fabric from a toy horse, shaping a dough‑like material, opening a chip bag, cutting paper into shapes, shaking paper with shears, measuring with a tape, and finally picking up a blue pen to draw measurement marks on a small mask before dropping it onto the desk. Throughout the segment the warm, yellow‑lit room and the shelves filled with various objects remain visible.

summary.brief: The creator walks through a rapid series of small‑craft actions, mainly folding, cutting and handling paper while also peeling tape, unwrapping a knife and tying thread.
summary.detailed: A man in a red shirt with a tattoo on his left forearm works at a kitchen table. He begins by folding a yellow sheet of paper like a booklet, lifting the left side, flipping the page to show the opposite side, and refolding it repeatedly. He then positions parts of a tiny cardboard house, switches to scissors (and occasionally pliers) to cut out drawn shapes from the folded paper, and tears sections as if with a scalpel. A strip of tape is peeled away from the paper, and later he removes a plastic wrapper from a new knife. Short interludes show him repairing a torn bill with tape, briefly attempting a balloon figure, trying to open a wine bottle, and ripping two pieces of paper attached to a stick. Finally, he pulls a loop of thread through a knot, rolls string around a knotted object, and performs a quick hand‑over‑object motion before the video ends. Throughout, shelves loaded with blue cups, bowls and picture frames are visible in the background.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: corset pattern tutorial 3 (BJD Dollfie Sewing)
summary_sent_to_llm.description: Part Three of the Corset Pattern tutorial.
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The presenter, a man in a red shirt with a pentagram tattoo on his left forearm, removes a yellow‑gauze cast from a miniature doll and cuts the back of the cast in half. He then slices the remaining paper into the individual corset pieces, turning some face‑up and others face‑down as required. Each piece is numbered sequentially from the front (1, 2, 3, …) and arrows are drawn to indicate the correct orientation. He adds seam‑allowance lines based on his sewing‑machine allowance, then cuts the pieces precisely along those lines. After the pattern is prepared, he shows a row of five yellow paper strips, counts them while pointing, and holds up a shoe for comparison. The tutorial concludes with a close‑up of him holding a Barbie doll while looking away.
action_list: Count paper strips and show boot
Remove fabric, detach head, and mark sculpture
Mark and write on pattern pieces
Pick up and examine paper strips
Cut torso pattern and trim sock

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
